oliver: opened PR to clarify embedding sharding + vector-size mismatch guidance in the model catalog for nebula-3b and to add a short SDK example for client-side shard/merge. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6320

oliver: summary: users hit silent failures when they split long documents into shards but accidentally used the wrong dimension (e.g., 1536 vs 1530 after an old quant pipeline). asks: (1) add a clear compatibility row in nebula-3b card about embedding dimensionality and aliasing, (2) include a tiny bench table for embed throughput with and without sharding, and (3) add short python/js snippets for sharding + reassemble helpers for the SDK.

kei: thanks. runtime note: the model emits 1536-d vectors (nebula-3b and nebula-3b-lite variants) always. older SDK clients sometimes applied a PCA postprocess leaving 1530 which causes downstream cosine mismatches. we should call out "vector-dim: 1536" explicitly and recommend verifying shape in client.

bina: bench I ran: single-request embed throughput (avg tokens/sec): nebula-3b fp16: 420 t/s, nebula-3b-q4_cpu: 120 t/s. With client-side 4-shard parallelization measured end-to-end: fp16: 1600 t/s (approx), q4_cpu: 420 t/s. Pasted compact table into PR.

oliver: added a compatibility row: "Embeddings: output_dim=1536. If you shard inputs, ensure merge uses length-weighted averaging and preserves order; mismatched dims cause silent downstream errors." added a small example but lint flagged duplicate anchor.

lint-bot: ERROR docs/models/nebula-3b.md: anchor "embedding-guidance" already defined in docs/models/polaris-13b.md line 34.

maya: prefer model-scoped anchors like "nebula3b-emb-guidance". also suggest adding a one-line FAQ for customers who use third-party PCA to mention re-processing.

oliver: updated anchor to nebula3b-emb-guidance and added short FAQ: "If you previously applied PCA/quantization that changes dimension, re-run alignment tests (sample pairs + cosine threshold) or prefer server-side sharding. See embedding tests in the evals repo."

kei: SDK snippet suggestion (python) for sharding + merge:```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import numpy as np

client = RedwoodClient()
texts = ["very long doc ..."]
shards = [texts[i::4] for i in range(4)]
results = []
for s in shards:
    r = client.embed(model="nebula-3b", input=s)
    results.append(r.vectors)
# merge: length-weighted average (example)
def merge_vectors(vlist, lengths):
    weighted = sum(v * l for v, l in zip(vlist, lengths)) / sum(lengths)
    return weighted

merged = merge_vectors([np.mean(r, axis=0) for r in results], [len(s) for s in shards])
print(merged.shape)  # (1536,)```

ke i: small JS example too (async):```js
const client = new RedwoodClient()
const shards = splitTextIntoShards(doc, 4)
const promises = shards.map(s => client.embed({ model: 'nebula-3b', input: s }))
const res = await Promise.all(promises)
const vectors = res.map(r => average(r.vectors))
const merged = weightedAverage(vectors, shards.map(s => s.length))
console.log(merged.length) // 1536
```

bina: runtime nit: call out exact variant names where dims are consistent: nebula-3b, nebula-3b-lite, nebula-3b-quant. Also mention that some legacy export pipelines produced 1530-d vectors — link to migration notes.
